summary: Release-tooling fix in scripts/sync-lockstep-versions.mjs. At the base, bumpCargoPackageVersion threw 'did not find a version line' whenever the crate was already at the target version: String.replace returned an identical string, and the code took that to mean the line was missing. Because the root `version` script (changeset version && node scripts/sync-lockstep-versions.mjs) runs on every release, any release that did not bump @cipherstash/eql failed at this step. At head the function checks that a version line exists before it replaces anything, so an unchanged version returns the manifest as it was. A missing version line still throws. The new unit test pins the no-op case, and the existing test for a missing version line is unchanged. The only release-risk consequence is that non-EQL releases now reach the later steps of the hook (Cargo.lock refresh, skew-gated SQL asset preparation), which those releases could not reach before. Those steps were designed to run on every release, and they fail loudly rather than silently. Impact is low. Normal review is enough.

behaviour_changes.description: bumpCargoPackageVersion no longer throws when the [package] version already equals the target. It returns the input unchanged. The error for a [package] section without a version line now comes from an explicit regex test that runs before the replace, not from comparing the strings afterwards.

On a release that does not change EQL's version, `pnpm run version` no longer aborts in step 2 of the lockstep hook. It continues to the Cargo.lock refresh (cargo update -p eql-bindings in each lock workspace) and to prepareBindingAssets, which skips the SQL rebuild when eqlLockstepSkew finds no disagreement.
Adds a unit test asserting that bumpCargoPackageVersion(CARGO, '0.4.2') returns CARGO unchanged.

failure_scenarios.title: Non-EQL releases now reach the lock refresh and skew-gated asset steps that they previously never ran
failure_scenarios.trigger: A release with changesets that do not bump @cipherstash/eql, so the crate is already at V (3.0.5 at head) when the hook runs.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: At the base, the hook threw in step 2 for an unchanged version, so steps 3 and 4 never ran on a non-EQL release. At head, step 2 is a no-op and main() goes on to run `mise exec -- cargo update --package eql-bindings` against every discovered lock, then prepareBindingAssets. If the tree carries any lockstep skew at an unchanged version (a manifest, digest or SQL stamp that disagrees), prepareBindingAssets rebuilds the SQL under an already released number. AGENTS.md says that can produce a digest the registry does not carry, which then trips the release gate. A failure in cargo or mise in the release job would also stop the version step.
failure_scenarios.consequence: In the worst case the release job fails loudly at the version step or at the gate, and no Version Packages commit or publish happens. Nothing silent or irreversible results. The base already failed every non-EQL release at this step, so this is not a regression against the base.

evidence.claim: At the base, the function throws 'did not find a version line' whenever replace() leaves the section unchanged, which also happens when the version already matches.
At head, the function tests for the version line before replacing and returns the input unchanged when the version already matches.
main() writes the bump result, then refreshes every discovered Cargo.lock, then calls prepareBindingAssets.
prepareBindingAssets skips the rebuild when eqlLockstepSkew finds no skew, and throws if skew remains after a rebuild.
The root version script is `changeset version && node scripts/sync-lockstep-versions.mjs`.
The hook runs on every release, and an asset rebuild under an unchanged version can trip the release gate's frozen-bytes-skew check.
Tests cover the missing-section and missing-version-line errors and the new unchanged-version no-op.
CI runs `pnpm run test:scripts`, which includes scripts/__tests__.
